summary: Decision: libdvi (PIO) DVI, 320x240 fb hardware-doubled to 640x480
description: RESOLVED. HDMI is wired to GPIO32-39, but HSTX is hardwired to GPIO12-19 only, so HSTX CANNOT drive this board's HDMI -- libdvi (Wren6991/PicoDVI, PIO) is mandatory, matching Waveshare's reference demo. Framebuffer = 320x240 RGB565 (~154KB, fits 520KB SRAM); libdvi scans out pixel/line-doubled (DVI_VERTICAL_REPEAT=2) to 640x480p 60Hz. CoCo 256x192 centers in 320x240 -> 512x384 with blank borders on screen. Config = pico_sock_cfg, invert_diffpairs=false, pio_set_gpio_base(pio,16). See README.md.

summary: DEFERRED: reconcile DVI (~252MHz) vs PIO-USB (120/240MHz) system clock
description: DEFERRED to the USB phase (PIZERO-11+). Decision: prove XRoar rendering first by running DVI at its native ~252MHz TMDS clock (close to the AMOLED port's 250MHz, so emulation gets full headroom and no clock compromise). The conflict only matters once USB host is added: libdvi 640x480p60 needs sys ~252MHz, Pico-PIO-USB needs exactly 120/240MHz (252/48 is fractional -> USB jitter). A custom DVI driver would NOT help -- the bit-rate=sysclk coupling is inherent to PIO DVI. When revisited: feed libdvi a 240MHz-friendly 640x480 timing (24MHz pixel clock ~57Hz, monitor-tolerated) so USB is happy, and verify on a real monitor. [IN-PROGRESS 2026-05-28: spike on path 1 -- sysclk 252->240 MHz with a custom 640x480 timing at 24 MHz pixel clock (~57.14 Hz refresh). Unblocks PIZERO-11.] [DONE 2026-05-28: path 1 verified on hardware. sysclk 240 MHz, custom 640x480 timing at 24 MHz pixel clock (~57.14 Hz refresh) -- monitor accepts, BASIC boots normally, emulator still hits 60 fps (decoupled from display refresh via FRAME_PERIOD_US). summary: PIO-USB host bring-up: enumerate a USB keyboard
description:
DONE 2026-05-29 on hardware. Pico-PIO-USB host on the PIO-USB port (D+=28 / D-=29) brought up via Adafruit_TinyUSB, host stack on PIO 1 (libdvi owns PIO 0). Three fixes were needed for a clean enumeration + report flow:

(1) Initialize USB host BEFORE multicore_launch_core1 — alarm_pool_create() spins forever if core 1 is already inside libdvi's DMA-IRQ loop. Init while core 1 is idle, then launch libdvi.

(2) Add -DCFG_TUH_HID_EPIN_BUFSIZE=64 / EPOUT_BUFSIZE=64 to build flags so TinyUSB has a place to land incoming HID reports.

(3) Call tuh_hid_set_default_protocol(HID_PROTOCOL_BOOT) BEFORE USBHost.begin() — common wireless keyboard/mouse dongles need to be talked to in boot protocol for reports to flow without report-descriptor parsing. Doing it via set_default (pre-mount) keeps both interfaces mounting cleanly; trying it via set_protocol AFTER mount breaks the second interface.

Verified: USB-A wireless dongle enumerates (VID:PID 05ac:0256), two interfaces mount (idx=0 boot mouse, idx=1 generic), and [usb] HID report lines stream 8-byte boot-keyboard reports as keys are pressed (e.g. 0x2C = space). PIZERO-12 (HID -> DSCAN) picks up from here.

KNOWN CAVEAT: not all USB devices enumerate — modern USB 2.0 high-speed keyboards/mice (e.g. Keychron K2, standalone gaming mice) do not work with PIO-USB's 1.1-only stack. Period-correct simple wired USB keyboards or wireless USB receivers are the compatible class.

summary: Map USB HID keycodes -> CoCo keyboard matrix
description:
DONE 2026-05-29 on hardware. USB HID boot-keyboard reports are translated into CoCo DSCAN codes and injected via the existing coco_machine_press_key()/release_key() matrix hooks. Verified: typing PRINT "HI" + Enter on a USB keyboard via the wireless dongle yields the expected output in Color BASIC on the HDMI display.

Implementation in src/main.cpp: (1) static 256-entry hid_to_dscan[] lookup mapping HID usage codes to CoCo K_* values with 0xFF sentinel for unmapped; (2) hid_keyboard_apply() diffs the current 6-byte HID keycode set against the previous and issues press/release events for transitions, plus shift modifier handling (HID bits 1/5 of byte 0); (3) per-key release in pump_keyboard() so autotype/serial input no longer clears USB-held keys via release_all_keys().

Notes: works around our test dongle mislabeling its keyboard interface as proto=2 (mouse) by treating any 8-byte report as a boot-keyboard report regardless of declared protocol. tuh_hid_set_default_protocol(HID_PROTOCOL_BOOT) (PIZERO-11) keeps incoming reports in the predictable 8-byte format.

summary: Custom wavetable/sampled-voice synth device (Blofeld-style) for the CoCo
description:
[REFRAMED 2026-07-19: the goal is NOT to emulate a classic chip (those are already emulated elsewhere) but to build an ORIGINAL synth engine as a CoCo sound device -- specifically a WAVETABLE + SAMPLED-VOICE engine in the spirit of the Waldorf Blofeld (morphing wavetables, per-voice multimode filter, envelopes/LFOs). The old AMY/AY/SID framing is kept at the bottom as reference alternatives only.] OUTPUT PATH NOW EXISTS: PIZERO-18's 48 kHz/16-bit SPSC-ring -> HDMI data-island path shipped (PIZERO-35/45), so the old hard dependency is satisfied. The synth generates NATIVELY at 48 kHz (no resampling, unlike the tick-keyed CoCo DAC), mixes with the CoCo audio in audio_emit (coco_machine.cpp), and rides the existing ring out to HDMI. PLACEMENT: runs on CORE 0 (where CoCo audio is already produced); core 1 is full (DVI TMDS encode + scanout + USB + SD servicing), no room. BUDGET (measured, README perf table): core-0 per 16.67 ms frame = ~11.5 ms used (emu 9.4 + render 0.56 + blit 1.5), ~5.3 ms (31%) FREE -- but that free slice is ALSO the frame-drop safety margin and the SAM high-speed-POKE ceiling (PIZERO-48), so budget only ~3-4 ms/frame for synth. At ~3.5 ms/frame that is ~880k cyc/frame / 800 samples = ~1100 cyc/sample for the WHOLE synth -> rough polyphony: ~10 voices at 100 cyc/sample (wavetable+lin-interp+ADSR), ~7 at 150 (+resonant filter+wave morph), ~4-5 at 250 (Blofeld-grade: 2D wavetable interp + multimode filter + 2 env + LFOs). Confirm the real cycles/voice via the PIZERO-58 bench BEFORE committing. Synth cost is CONSTANT/predictable per active voice (unlike emulation), so use a CONFIGURABLE VOICE CAP + graceful degradation (drop voices / simpler interp when a frame runs long). COMPUTE: RP2350 M33 cores have single-precision FPU + DSP/SIMD -> float wavetables/filters (~1-3 cyc/op) OR Q15 fixed with DSP MACs; pick per the bench. MEMORY IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT (not CPU): SRAM is ~89-94% used (double-buffer video + the audio ring) leaving only tens of KB, and the PSRAM pad is UNPOPULATED on this board -- so wavetables/samples CANNOT live in SRAM. They live in the 16 MB FLASH (ample), read via XIP; for the hot per-sample loop MIRROR only the active wave frame(s) into SRAM (~1 KB: current+next morph frame, 256 samples x 2 B each) so XIP cache-miss jitter never hits the inner loop. SAMPLED/PCM VOICES are the tricky bit: sequential playback has OK XIP locality but PITCHED (interpolated, non-unity-rate) playback wanders flash and can thrash the cache -> add a small SRAM prefetch/DMA window per playing sample; PROTOTYPE this before committing. Loading NEW banks from SD at runtime = flash PROGRAMMING, which STALLS XIP on both cores (video hiccup) -> do bank loads only at a 'load' moment (BIOS action / between titles), never mid-performance; bank SWITCHING within already-flashed data is just a pointer change (free). CONTROL SURFACE (this is the 'design your own engine' part): intercept guest bus writes to a chosen address range into a synth register file (same trick as the PIZERO-55 $FFB0 palette interception, or branch coco_machine like the VDG hookup); YOU define the register map -- note on/off/pitch, wavetable select, morph position, envelope, filter cutoff/res, LFO routing. Guest writes are tick-keyed; render the synth in SUB-BLOCKS (e.g. 8 x 100 samples ~= 2 ms) so control latency feels instrument-tight. Gate behind a build flag; RAM is the gating constraint so measure RAM cost too. DEPENDS ON: PIZERO-58 (voice-budget bench, do first). Cross-link docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/hdmi-audio-notes.md, PIZERO-55 (shared bus-interception mechanism). Verify on hw: N-voice patch plays via a $range poke, correct pitch, fps stays 60 / core-0 frame < 16.67 ms, no video hiccup.

---
[PRIOR FRAMING kept for reference -- classic-chip alternatives, superseded by the custom-engine goal above:] Companion to PIZERO-16 (alternate video): add an optional synth/sound-chip 'sound board' for the CoCo, beyond the native 6-bit DAC + single-bit sound XRoar already emulates. PRIMARY candidate: AMY (shorepine/amy), a fixed-point MCU synth library that runs on RP2350 (Arduino support for ESP32-S3/RP2040/RP2350/Teensy; AMYboard hardware is ESP32-S3 but the engine is portable). AMY gives virtual-analog (Juno-6), FM (DX7 6-op), partial/breakpoint (Alles/Atari AMY), wavetable/PCM sampler, and an 808-style drum machine -- expose a few as an alternate sound device. Discrete-chip alternatives (portable C cores): AY-3-8910/YM2149 (libayemu, emu2149 -- cheap, period-correct), SID 6581/8580 (reSID heavy; lighter reimpls -- aspirational), YM2612/SN76489 (libOPNMIDI, ymfm -- FM, cycle-hungry). RP2350 reference: Datanoise PicoADK v2.

PREREQUISITE DECISIONS (gate the work):
1. Audio output path -- our Waveshare board has no audio DAC and libdvi isn't set up for HDMI audio. Choose PWM audio, I2S to an external DAC, or add HDMI audio islands to libdvi. Decide first (analogous to the PIZERO-02b clock decision for video).
2. CPU/core budget -- core0 ~11.5/16.76ms at 60fps, core1 owned by libdvi scanout (+ future USB host). AMY/AY are affordable, SID/FM are not. Likely generate a fixed sample-block per frame on whichever core has slack.

Implementation sketch: a synth/sound device fed either by a bus-addressable register interface (chip emulation, branch coco_machine like the VDG hookup) or by a higher-level note API (AMY). References captured in chat 2026-05-27.

summary: USB hot-replug does not re-enumerate after disconnect
description:
OPEN / UNDIAGNOSED. Symptom: USB devices enumerate only on a cold boot with the device already attached; unplugging and re-plugging (or hot-plugging a new device) does not re-enumerate.

NO CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE — nothing has been tested or verified. Two UNVERIFIED hypotheses have been raised, neither reproduced or ruled out:
  (1) Power: insufficient VBUS / inrush current from the development USB-C port. Would predict that powering the board from a battery / powered hub makes hot-replug work. UNTESTED.
  (2) Software: RP2350-E9 input leakage masking the unplug, plus the Pico-PIO-USB state machine holding the J line, so the disconnect event is never seen. UNVERIFIED.

(History note 2026-06-01: an earlier revision of this issue asserted the power hypothesis as a confirmed 'root cause found via user diagnostic'. That was an agent assumption, not a tested result — corrected here to avoid a misleading record.)

NEXT STEP when revisited: actually test. Power from a battery / powered hub and hot-replug; instrument the PIO-USB connection-state path to see whether a disconnect event is ever delivered; bisect power vs software before claiming either.

References for a future deep dive:
  - RP2350-E9: https://hackaday.com/2024/09/20/raspberry-pi-rp2350-e9-erratum-redefined-as-input-mode-leakage-current/
  - tinyusb #3296: https://github.com/hathach/tinyusb/issues/3296 [OBS 2026-06-04 (during PIZERO-29 HDMI work): reproduced the warm-vs-cold distinction -- after a picotool warm reboot (-x) the USB keyboard does NOT enumerate (emulation runs but no input -> game frozen); a COLD power-cycle enumerates it fine. Data point only, NOT a diagnosis: warm-vs-cold points at USB/PIO-USB reset state rather than power, but still UNTESTED and deferred per user.] [2026-06-06: likely surfaces as a CURSOR/SYSTEM FREEZE when typing under load (e.g. a few SOUND commands) with the USB keyboard enumerated (usb=1). Same load driven over the serial console (usb=0) never wedges -> implicates the USB host path. To confirm: when frozen, check whether the [run] serial log goes SILENT (core0 stuck in USBHost.task) vs keeps printing.] [2026-06-06: USER reports REGULAR freezes over the past few days (pre-dates the PIZERO-31 timer fix, confirming it's a standing stability issue, not the timer work). Watching for a repro to capture: when frozen, leave powered and check the [run] serial log -- SILENT = core0 stuck in USBHost.task (USB). Promote priority if it keeps recurring.]

[2026-06-08: another hard hang during PIZERO-41 debugging -- board dropped USB completely (no CDC, no BOOTSEL) under repeated flash/reset cycles; only a physical power-cycle recovered it. Also consistently saw usb=0 (USB keyboard not enumerated) after WARM flash-reboots throughout the session, needing serial-console input instead. Keeps recurring -> consider promoting priority; PIZERO-33 watchdog is the diagnostic path.]

[2026-06-28 PROMOTED to high + in-progress at user request -- hotplug is now the priority and it also gates reliable USB-gamepad testing (PIZERO-13): without re-enumeration the user must cold-boot with the controller attached. ATTACK PLAN is diagnostic-first (can't fix blind): (1) capture the boot line 'RP2350 chip_id=.. revision=N (E9 workaround active: yes/NO)' (main.cpp:787) -- directly tests the leading hypothesis (E9 input-leakage masking disconnect so the host never sees the unplug; the cold-vs-warm asymmetry fits this); (2) add ~1Hz instrumentation of PIO-USB root-port line/connection state + g_usb_devices into the [run] telemetry to see whether a connect/disconnect event is EVER delivered after boot; (3) hardware bisect -- power from battery/powered hub and retry, and check docs/RP2350-PiZero-schematic.pdf for host-side 15k pull-downs on D+/D- that PIO-USB disconnect detection needs; (4) only then attempt a flag-gated periodic root-port reset / re-enumeration when unmounted (tinyusb#3296 workaround), guarded so it can't wedge the shared PIO1 (this path is the PIZERO-33 freeze suspect). Honest expectation: may need a hardware change (hub/pull-downs), not just software.]

[2026-06-28 DIAGNOSED ON HARDWARE -- root cause confirmed via instrumented build (src/usb_hotplug_diag.c shim over pio_usb_ll.h: line_state + root_port.connected/is_fullspeed/event/ep_error/ints; main.cpp [run] line + per-frame [usb-evt] edge log + HID rpts/rfail counters). FINDINGS: (1) This board is RP2350 revision=3 and PIO-USB's RP2350-E9 input-leakage workaround is COMPILED OUT -- pio_usb_bus_get_line_state() gates the drain on chip_version<=2 only (boot line: 'revision=3 (E9 workaround active: NO)'). (2) The disconnect is masked at the LINE layer: once a device enumerates, PIO-USB's TX state machine pins D+/D- at J/FS, so line_state + the debounced root_port.connected flag NEVER change on unplug. 75s capture with a real unplug+replug = ZERO change (ls=J/FS conn=1 usb=1 flat throughout, no [usb-evt], no umount cb, no ep_error). The host drives the bus, so line-state/connected are electrically blind to the device. (3) The line CAN read SE0 only while the SM is released: the [usb-evt] log caught J/FS->SE0->J/FS during the boot RESET sequence, then it pins J/FS after enumeration. (4) usb= mount count is therefore a PHANTOM after any hotplug -- it reflects whatever enumerated at cold boot and never updates (observed: usb=1 conn=1 for 90s while a hot-swapped keyboard sat unpolled at rpts=0). CONCLUSION: this RULES OUT the 'TinyUSB sees the disconnect but fails to re-enumerate' theory -- the event never reaches the stack. RULES IN the line-masking cause (rev3 E9-workaround-off + SM-holds-J). WORKING PATH CONFIRMED: cold-boot with the keyboard attached enumerates cleanly (composite kbd: idx0 proto=1 keyboard + idx1/idx2 generic) and keystrokes flow (rpts 0->101, rfail=0, eperr=0). FIX DIRECTIONS to try next (not line-state based, since that's blind): (a) re-enable the E9 drain in get_line_state regardless of rev (patch the vendored lib or pre-drain) and see if SE0 becomes detectable post-enumeration; (b) detect device-gone from TRANSFER errors (HID IN polls NAK/timeout once removed) and trigger pio_usb_host_stop()/restart() to re-enumerate; (c) hardware: confirm host-side 15k D+/D- pull-downs in docs/RP2350-PiZero-schematic.pdf, try a powered hub. NOTE: unplug did NOT freeze the board (fps stayed 60) -> the PIZERO-33 freeze is a SEPARATE event, not caused by unplug per se.]

[2026-06-29 KEY MECHANISM FOUND (HW-confirmed, user-verified timing) -- and it INVALIDATES the 'detect via transfer errors' fix path. Experiment: cold-boot with keyboard (working, rpts climbs on keypress), then UNPLUG at ~23s, then REPLUG at ~45s, watching the rpts/rfail/eperr/ints counters. RESULT: on unplug, instead of errors or a stall, the HID report stream EXPLODES into a steady ~180 reports/SECOND phantom flood (rpts 298 -> 7126 at a dead-constant +180/s for the rest of the capture) with rfail=0, eperr=0, ints=0, conn=1, ls=J/FS THROUGHOUT. PIO-USB keeps polling the now-device-less bus, decodes the SM-held J idle line as a valid IN response, and 'completes' a HID transfer ~180x/s forever. The REPLUG at ~45s was ALSO invisible: the flood continued with zero discontinuity, no [usb] device attached, no re-enum -> reproduces 'reattached devices not noticed' exactly. CONSEQUENCES: (a) line_state/connected/event/ep_error/ints are ALL useless as a disconnect signal here (confirmed flat) -> fix paths (a) E9-drain and (b) transfer-error-detection are DEAD: the line is actively DRIVEN to J by the SM (not floating-high from leakage), so the E9 drain can't reveal SE0 post-enumeration, and there are no errors to catch. (b) The phantom flood IS the detectable signature: a real boot keyboard sends reports ONLY on key transitions, so a high steady rate of reports -- especially byte-IDENTICAL ones -- means the device is gone. NEW FIX DESIGN (the first data-grounded one): in tuh_hid_report_received_cb, track consecutive byte-identical reports per interface; when >=N identical arrive in a row (phantom flood, N ~ 50-100), declare disconnect and trigger a root-port re-enumeration via pio_usb_host_stop() + pio_usb_host_restart() (both exist in pio_usb.h). Gate behind a flag; keep it OFF the freeze-prone hot path (PIZERO-33); a real working device never trips it (its reports change or stop). On re-enum, a freshly-attached OR replugged device mounts cleanly. RISK: stop/restart on the shared PIO1 while libdvi runs on PIO0/core1 must not wedge -- validate carefully. Instrumentation to add for implementing: log the report PAYLOAD bytes to confirm phantom reports are identical/empty (current build only counts them). Diagnostic build state: src/usb_hotplug_diag.c + main.cpp counters + platformio.ini src-filter entry are committed-to-working-tree (NOT yet a flag); curate per PIZERO-42 once the fix lands.]

description:
Make the CoCo actually make sound. XRoar already emulates the 6-bit DAC + single-bit cassette/speaker tap internally, but nothing on this board drives those samples to an output -- the PiZero is currently silent. Filed after the 43b reconciliation (2026-05-31): 43b treats native audio as a first-class deliverable (COCO-7 decision -> COCO-19 implementation, see its docs/audio-decision.md), and that split is the transferable lesson. This issue is the basic, in-scope audio path; PIZERO-17 (synth/sound-chip device) is a separate far-future stretch that DEPENDS on the output path decided here.

GATE (decide first, analogous to PIZERO-02b's clock decision; full feasibility scoping in docs/audio-decision.md):
Choose the audio output sink. PRIMARY candidate: HDMI audio data-island packets emitted by libdvi -- sound over the single existing cable, no extra hardware (needs libdvi data-island support, which it currently lacks; investigate cost vs the 240 MHz / 24 MHz-pixel-clock timing already in use). FALLBACK: PWM to a free GPIO + RC filter or a small Class-D amp (simplest, needs a wire/part). Decide before implementing.

IMPLEMENTATION SKETCH: tap XRoar's sound_module / DAC output, generate a fixed PCM sample-block per frame (CoCo native rate) on whichever core has slack (core0 has ~5ms headroom of the 16.76ms budget; core1 is owned by libdvi scanout), feed the chosen sink. Verify on hardware: audible BASIC SOUND / PLAY / key-click at correct pitch with core0 frame time staying under 16.76ms.

summary: Programmable VDG palette (GIME-style palette registers)
description: [SUPERSEDED 2026-07-19 by PIZERO-55, which subsumes this as its Part 1 and adds a BIOS palette editor + per-title .pal profiles. This ticket's unique mechanisms (guest-side $FFB0-$FFBF bus-write interception so CoCo-3-aware recolor pokes work live; default=stock-palette transparency; the PIZERO-15 glyph-LUT rebuild-on-write wrinkle; GIME-address mirroring; the GIME default slot->color verify TODO) have been folded into PIZERO-55. Closed as superseded -- see PIZERO-55.] ORIGINAL: Augment the native MC6847 VDG with a programmable color palette instead of bolting on a foreign video chip -- the preferred, faithful 'extend the VDG' direction (split out of PIZERO-16, which stays as the heavier full-alternate-video track). MECHANISM: a 16-entry palette register file mirroring the real GIME palette addresses $FFB0-$FFBF (6-bit R-G-B, 2 bits/channel = 16 colors from 64). Intercept writes to that range on the CoCo bus; the VDG renderers (render_alpha/render_graphics/render_rg6 in lib/coco_machine) emit palette[index] -> RGB565 instead of fixed CoCo color constants. DEFAULT palette = the stock CoCo colors, so unmodified games look exactly like a normal CoCo and the feature is completely transparent until a program POKEs the registers. AUTHENTICITY: this mirrors a real CoCo 3 behavior -- in GIME VDG-compatible mode, classic VDG-mode colors route through palette RAM and can be recolored live via $FFB0+ pokes; a recolor program would behave the same here as on real CoCo 3 hardware. DECISIONS: (1) depth -- accept authentic 6-bit at $FFB0-$FFBF AND optionally expose an extended RGB565 palette at our own addresses for beyond-hardware color; (2) modes -- text/semigraphics/CG are index-based and the natural fit; RG6/PMODE4 artifact color is emergent from bit patterns, so palette there means redefining the endpoints (a separate, later mechanism); (3) mirror GIME addresses so CoCo-3-aware code just works. BOUNDARY: this is VDG+palette only, NOT full GIME/CoCo3 -- no hi-res GIME bitmap modes, no extra RAM/MMU, no hardware scroll, no GIME interrupts (those remain PIZERO-16). IMPLEMENTATION WRINKLE: PIZERO-15 precomputes glyph->packed-word LUTs with colors baked in; a palette write must rebuild those small LUTs (cheap -- palette writes are rare, once per screen not per frame). TODO before coding: verify the exact GIME VDG-compatible default slot->color mapping against GIME docs rather than guessing. Product context in docs/product-plan.md (the 'open platform you can extend' story; our homebrew game showcases it).

summary: HDMI data-island encoder core (TERC4 + BCH + packet framing)
description: M1 of PIZERO-18 (B) HDMI audio sink. The bedrock, host-validatable with NO board (like the PIZERO-18 (A) WAV host-test). Build a standalone encoder: (1) TERC4 4-bit->10-bit symbol LUT; (2) BCH ECC for the packet header + 4 subpacket ECC bytes (HDMI 1.4 packet structure); (3) framing for the mandatory packets -- General Control Packet (GCP), AVI InfoFrame, Audio InfoFrame, Audio Clock Regeneration (ACR; at our 24 MHz pixel clock 32 kHz -> N=4096 CTS=24000), and Audio Sample Packet (IEC 60958 subframes). Validate on the host against HDMI-spec test vectors / the shuichitakano PicoDVI-audio fork before any integration. Pure data transformation -> no timing risk here; this de-risks the most mechanical part. Parent: PIZERO-18. Blocks PIZERO-28.\n\n[BUILT + HOST-VALIDATED 2026-06-03. New lib/libdvi/dvi_data_island.{h,c} (pure C, no SDK deps -> builds on host and firmware). BCH generator determined deterministically by brute force to match the reference table: LSB-first, poly 0x83 (HDMI ECC). Host test (/tmp/di_test.c, includes the .c to see static bch_table) ALL PASS: (1) bch_table[0..15] == reference bytes; (2) BCH is a real ECC -- remainder of data||parity == 0 for header and all 4 subpackets; (3) ACR carries CTS=24000 N=4096 (32 kHz @ 24 MHz pixel clock); (4) AVI + Audio InfoFrame CEA checksums == 0; Audio InfoFrame SF/SS = 0x05 (32k/16-bit); (5) all 16 TERC4 symbols match binary spec + guard band 0x133; (6) header TERC4 round-trip -- reconstructed all 32 header bits from lane-0 nibble bit2. Compiles in firmware build (GC'd while unused -> 0 RAM until M2). NOT YET wired into libdvi -- that is M2 (PIZERO-28). NOTE: audio-sample IEC 60958 bit positions are best-effort and get verified on the sink in M4 (PIZERO-30).]

summary: Inject benign data island into libdvi blanking without breaking sync
description:
M2 of PIZERO-18 (B). Extend struct dvi_scanline_dma_list with data-island blocks (preamble -> leading guard band -> TERC4 island -> trailing guard band) on ALL THREE lanes, added as extra CHAIN_TO links in the per-scanline DMA chain. CRITICAL: keep the SINGLE back-porch IRQ per scanline -- do NOT take per-block IRQs -- which dodges the documented guard-band hazard (dvi_timing.cpp:191). Pre-encode the per-line packet into a small TERC4 buffer (same pattern as TMDS scanline encoding). For this milestone inject only a NULL/benign packet during blanking. HARDWARE ACCEPTANCE (first monitor test): video stays rock-solid and in sync, fps still 60. RAM: grown DMA lists ~1 KB + packet buffers ~1-2 KB, fits the ~30 KB free. Depends on PIZERO-27. Parent PIZERO-18.

[DESIGN REFINED 2026-06-03 (two de-risking changes vs the original framing): (1) inject during VERTICAL blanking first, not active-line hblank -- vblank lines carry no visible video, so a malformed island cannot corrupt the picture; if the monitor stays synced the mechanism is proven at near-zero risk. (2) BUFFER-SWAP not DMA-restructure: the vblank 'active' region's DMA block already supports pointing at a non-repeating 640px buffer (same as video lines), so fill a per-lane island-line buffer [control fill -> data-island preamble (8px) -> leading guard (2px) -> TERC4 island (32px) -> trailing guard (2px) -> control fill] and point the existing blocks at it. NO grown struct, NO new IRQs, does NOT touch the guard-band-hazard path. Pixel count identical. Budget: our timing h_fp=16/h_sync=96/h_bp=48 = 160px hblank; vblank lines fully blank (640+160 free). Will be flag-guarded (-DHDMI_DATA_ISLAND) so the known-good video path is the default and we can A/B. STILL NEEDED before coding: the fork's exact data-island PREAMBLE control symbols (CTL0-3 for the data-island period differ from the 4 basic vsync/hsync ctrl syms) and guard-band placement -- fetching shuichitakano/pico_lib's line-assembly (dvi.cpp) next.]

[HW RESULT 2026-06-04: implemented + flashed. Pipeline stayed healthy (fps 60, DMA/IRQ fine) BUT the monitor went BLACK with the island injected. Control-only diagnostic (swap buffer filled with pure control symbols, no island) -> VIDEO CORRECT. CONCLUSION: the buffer-swap/repoint mechanism is SOUND; the black screen was the island content. Root cause: you cannot half-do HDMI -- once a sink sees data-island preambles it expects full HDMI framing (video guard bands + preamble on ACTIVE lines + AVI InfoFrame), which our bare-DVI active lines lacked, so it rejected the signal. DECISION: merge M2+M3 -- convert the whole signal to HDMI (video preamble+guard on active lines via the same proven repoint, AND an AVI InfoFrame data island in vblank), then audio (M4). dvi_ctrl_syms confirmed = standard TMDS control tokens duplicated (0xd5354=(0x354<<10)|0x354), so get_ctrl_sym works directly for preambles. Mechanism (repoint blanking blocks at prepared buffers, no struct/IRQ change) carries forward to active lines too. [DONE 2026-06-04: merged into PIZERO-29 (full HDMI mode); the buffer-swap repoint mechanism was validated (control-only diagnostic = correct video) and HDMI-mode video confirmed correct on hardware.]

summary: HDMI audio ACR CTS depends on sink's pixel-clock assumption (V1.0 monitor compat)
description:
OPEN / V1.0 risk. AND HDMI_STD_TIMING (standard 25.2MHz pixel) also changed nothing. summary: Add core-1 watchdog / freeze detector to root-cause the recurring hangs
description:
OPEN. User reports REGULAR system freezes over the past few days (cursor freezes; pre-dates the PIZERO-31 timer fix, so it is a standing stability issue -- likely the PIZERO-11b USB-host path). Add an always-on, low-risk freeze detector so the NEXT freeze auto-dumps the smoking gun instead of needing a live catch. Design: core 1 (the DVI worker, which keeps running via DMA/PIO even if core 0 wedges) watches a core-0 heartbeat counter that loop() bumps each frame; if it stops advancing for ~1 s, dump over serial: core-0 PC, whether it is inside USBHost.task (set a 'in_usb_task' flag around the call), the libdvi SOF/frame counter, and millis(). Optionally arm the RP2350 hardware watchdog as a last-resort auto-reset (gated behind a flag so we can choose log-only vs reset). Keep it cheap and off the hot path. Parent PIZERO-11b.

[2026-06-08 DATA POINT: during PIZERO-41 audio-fidelity debugging (many flash/reset cycles + a WAV-dump build) the board HARD-HUNG and dropped off USB entirely -- no CDC serial port, not in BOOTSEL, invisible to picotool. A simple replug did NOT recover it; required a physical power-cycle (and was prone to needing BOOT-button BOOTSEL). This is exactly the freeze class this watchdog is meant to catch -- a clean repro of a hard hang that takes out USB. Reinforces priority.]

[2026-06-09 IN-PROGRESS -- user confirms freezes are the #1 everyday-use problem (minutes to a couple hours). Implementing a REVISED design (core 1 never returns from libdvi's scanout loop, so the original 'core-1 watches a heartbeat' is impractical without hacking libdvi). Instead: HARDWARE WATCHDOG petted from core 0 loop() -> auto-reboots a wedged board in WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_MS (default 3000ms) = auto-RECOVERY for everyday use. Plus PHASE MARKERS in watchdog scratch registers (survive a watchdog reset, cleared on power-on, guarded by WD_MAGIC in scratch[0]): scratch[1]=phase (SETUP/USBHost.task/emulate/render/blit/audio/pace), scratch[2]=heartbeat. On boot, if watchdog_caused_reboot() && magic matches, print '*** FREEZE RECOVERED *** stuck in <phase>' -> root-causes ACROSS the reset (confirms/denies the USB-host hypothesis). -DWATCHDOG_DISABLE leaves a freeze frozen for live debugging. src/main.cpp: includes + wd_phase/wd_heartbeat helpers + boot diagnosis + loop() arm/pet/markers. Build/flash pending.]

[2026-06-14 IMPLEMENTED + COMMITTED (4d49192); builds clean (pizero_stream RAM 70.4%). The repeated unflashable hangs are themselves strong evidence the watchdog (auto-reboot) is needed.]

summary: Re-architect HDMI audio delivery using Takano's reference (even per-active-line streaming)
description:
OPEN. Our packet ENCODER is already ported from shuichitakano/pico_lib dvi/data_packet.cpp (lib/libdvi/dvi_data_island.c -- TERC4/BCH/header/subpacket/ACR/InfoFrame), and it's sound. What we never adopted is his DELIVERY/SCHEDULING architecture -- where/when audio islands are placed in the scanline stream -- and that is the source of our residual frame-rate WARBLE.

STATE OF KNOWLEDGE (from this session):
* Pitch fixed via ACR CTS=25176 for the sink's assumed 25.175MHz clock (PIZERO-30/32).
* Source is clean (WAV-verified); the gap is HDMI DELIVERY, not the waveform/resampler.
* ACR cadence matters: 1/frame warbled; ~43/frame (every vblank line) audibly better (PIZERO-30).
* Active-line back-porch audio islands WORK on this sink; vblank BACK-PORCH islands BREAK video sync (PIZERO-34 -- even delivery via vblank is NOT viable here).
* Our limit is RAM: only ~77 pre-encoded per-line buffers of 480 active lines -> bursty delivery (audio bunched in active region, ~1.6ms gap during vblank) -> sink FIFO/PLL wobble at frame rate.

PLAN:
1. Read shuichitakano/pico_lib (and the RP2350 PicoDVI HDMI-audio ports) DELIVERY path: how he interleaves audio sample packets + ACR into the H-blanking of (nearly) every ACTIVE line, and how he encodes per-scanline rather than pre-allocating one buffer per line.
2. Adopt streaming/on-the-fly per-active-line audio encode so audio rides EVERY active line evenly (matching standard HDMI), sidestepping BOTH our buffer-count RAM cap AND the vblank-island sink rejection. Active-line audio already works on this sink, so this is the direction the sink accepts.
3. Re-examine 'Option A' (encode in the DMA IRQ) which blacked the screen early on -- determine whether that was a specific bug vs fundamental, and how he avoids it (which core, timing, handoff).
4. Keep the ACR-cadence fix; spread ACR per his cadence too.

ACCEPTANCE: synth-sine (HDMI_AUDIO_SYNTH) plays as a clean steady tone on the monitor (no frame-rate warble), real CoCo SOUND/PLAY sounds smooth, video rock-solid, RAM fits, core-0 frame budget holds. References: shuichitakano/pico_lib; PicoDVI HDMI-audio forks/RP2350 ports; rh1tech/FRANK (IEC framing, already matched). Supersedes the abandoned PIZERO-34 vblank approach.

[2026-06-07 PLAN + STAGED into PIZERO-36..40. KEY ARCHITECTURE FINDINGS from code review: (1) The per-line bp buffer is sized by the FIXED back porch (bpw = h_back_porch/DVI_SYMBOLS_PER_WORD ~= 65 words, dvi_timing.cpp:458), INDEPENDENT of packet count -- so the pre-encoded double-buffered banks g_la0/1/2[2][77][72] already cost ~130KB at 94% SRAM and the RAM lever is CARRIER-LINE COUNT, not packets/line. The bank model is structurally capped at ~77 lines (120 lines = +74KB, impossible). You CANNOT fix warble by adding carrier lines to the current model. (2) Therefore the only route to even per-line delivery within RAM is Takano's actual model: stop pre-allocating per line; encode ONE 16.16-metered audio packet per active line ON THE FLY in the DMA IRQ into a tiny rotating pool (~4 buffers, ~3.5KB). (3) The original 'Option A' IRQ-encode blackout is almost certainly flash latency: the encoder (dvi_di_encode_header/subpacket + dvi_terc4_syms) is FLASH-resident; moving it to RAM (PIZERO-37) is the surgical fix that makes IRQ encode viable. Spike-measure first (PIZERO-36). All behind -DHDMI_STREAM_AUDIO with the 77-line path as fallback. Plan: ~/.claude/plans/hi-whats-on-the-fluttering-quiche.md]

[2026-06-08 MEASURED (PIZERO-36 done) -- CORRECTS hypothesis (3) above. PIZERO-37 put the encoder in RAM, but a RAM-resident 1-packet encode still costs 4814 ns on HW, which is 89% of the 5420 ns back-porch window -> encoding in the back porch it ships in is STILL not viable even from RAM. So 'Option A' was never going to work as a same-line back-porch encode; flash latency made it worse but wasn't the whole story. THE viable design (4814ns = only 14% of the 33333ns full line): PIPELINE one line ahead -- while line N scans out, encode line N+1's island into a small rotating pool, in the core-1 line IRQ. ~480 enc/frame ~= 2.3ms (~12% of frame), affordable. This is now the hard constraint for PIZERO-38. PIZERO-37 HW-confirmed (audio build runs, fps=52). Stage 0/1 committed (65bb649).]

summary: Investigate full 60Hz HDMI output (monitor compat + correct game speed)
description:
OPEN / discussion. Current refresh = 24MHz pixel / (880x525) = ~51.95Hz -- off-spec; some monitors may reject a non-60Hz signal (consumer-QA exposure). KEY CLARIFICATION: this is NOT a render-speed limit -- core 0 has ~4ms/frame slack (cpu ~13.5ms of 19.25ms) and rendering a whole line at a time is cheap; the refresh is set by the TMDS timing (pixel clock x total pixels), independent of how fast we render the framebuffer. The 24MHz pixel = sysclk/10 and sysclk=240MHz is forced by PIO-USB (needs 120/240MHz).\n\nPaths to 60Hz:\n(a) PIO-USB at ~252MHz: sysclk 251.75MHz -> 25.175MHz pixel -> STANDARD 640x480p60 (800x525) AND keep USB. BEST outcome if PIO-USB tolerates ~252MHz (its bit-banging timing is calibrated for 120/240 -- UNCERTAIN; needs a HW experiment). FIRST EXPERIMENT: build 252MHz + true 800x525 60Hz timing + USB enabled; check DVI stable @60Hz and whether the USB keyboard enumerates.\n(b) Reduced-blanking 60Hz at 24MHz: 800x500 = exactly 60.0Hz, keeps USB, but vblank=20 lines is non-standard (CVT-RB-ish) -> may HURT monitor compat (opposite of the goal) and squeezes the audio-island back porch. Lower confidence.\n(c) USB-less standard timing: 252MHz + true 800x525 60Hz, universal monitor compat, but DISABLES USB keyboard/gamepad (PIO-USB) -> not shippable for a console. Diagnostic/fallback only.\n\n60Hz BONUSES beyond monitor compat: game speed becomes correct (CoCo NTSC = 59.92Hz; at 52Hz we run ~13% slow) and audio cadence simplifies (48000/60 = 800 samp/frame). NB: the off-spec 24MHz is also the root of PIZERO-41's source-side... no -- 41 is source-side, independent. Decide after the (a) PIO-USB-at-252MHz experiment, which is the highest-value test.

[2026-06-16 IN-PROGRESS -- Path (a) experiment built (env pizero_60hz, flag HDMI_60HZ_TEST): 252MHz sysclk (vreg 1.25) + true 800x525 timing @ 25.2MHz pixel = 60.0Hz + USB host ENABLED, on the no-audio base (the audio build's wide h_bp=130 can't fit in 800-total, so this test drops audio). summary: Document emulation pacing & CoCo high-speed (SAM double-speed) behavior
description: Write up how guest CPU speed-up holds up end-to-end, since the pacing model is non-obvious and the headroom limit is real. Key findings (verified in code): (1) No host fast-forward toggle; the only double-speed is the CoCo's own SAM high-speed POKE (POKE 65495/65497, address-dependent vs full), implemented in vendored XRoar mc6883.c (8 ticks/fast cycle vs 16). (2) coco_machine_run_cycles paces by FIXED EMULATED TIME per frame, not fixed instruction count: run_cpu_with_audio sets cycles_remaining = cycles*16 TICKS (coco_machine.cpp:793) and each mem access subtracts ncycles ticks (:486). So a frame always advances CYCLES_PER_FRAME*16 = 238640 ticks ~= 16.667ms emulated time regardless of SAM speed. (3) Therefore audio pitch and video are correct BY DESIGN (samples are tick-keyed -> still 800/frame in fast mode; no resampler distortion; the hdmi-audio-notes 'fast-forward distortion' was a separate startup ring-overflow bug). (4) The real limiter is core-0 host headroom: fast mode executes ~2x as many 6809 cycles within the same per-frame budget, so emulation host cost ~doubles (README perf ~9.4ms -> ~18.8ms est) and exceeds the 16.67ms frame budget (only ~31% slack at 1x). Pacing then resyncs/drops the deficit -> guest runs slower than 2x AND the audio ring under-produces vs the real-time core-1 consumer -> underruns after ~1s. Threshold ~1.6-1.7x: address-dependent (~1.3-1.5x) likely squeaks by; full ~2x overruns. Video stays 60Hz (decoupled core 1) but shows the lag. (5) Not yet characterized on-device -- next step is to measure via the per-second [run] fps/cpu/blit serial telemetry (PIZERO-15) under a tight high-speed-POKE loop, and decide whether to cap/ignore the full-speed bit. New doc docs/cpu-speed.md; cross-link from docs/pipeline.md and README Performance.

Authentic feel, sidesteps the USB CPU budget entirely (no hub needed), and lands in the same DAC-comparator injection API. Note the pots wire as dividers to 3.3V; only ADC0/ADC1 (GPIO26/27) are free, so one stick (X+Y) is clean but a second analog stick needs an external mux (74HC4051 or I2C ADC on I2C0 6/7). Connector exposes 5 signals: X wiper, Y wiper, +V (pot top rail), GND (pot bottom + button common), Fire (switch->GND). DIN-5 pin NUMBERING VARIES across CoCo1/2/3, left vs right port, 1- vs 2-button -- BUZZ OUT the actual connector with a multimeter, do not trust a pinout table (find wipers by watching R-to-rail change as the stick moves; button by continuity when pressed). KEY RULE: power the pot top rail from the board 3V3, NOT 5V -- each pot is just a divider, so 3V3 makes the wiper sweep 0-3.3V (exactly ADC range) and keeps 5V off the not-5V-tolerant GPIO; DO NOT connect the stick's original +5V wire. Wiring (one stick -> right/port 0): pot top->3V3; pot bottom/GND->GND; X wiper->GPIO26/ADC0; Y wiper->GPIO27/ADC1; Fire->GPIO3 (input, internal pull-up, active-low = LOW when pressed); optional 2nd button->any free GPIO (same pull-up+to-GND pattern). Only 6-bit needed (JOYSTK 0-63) so cap+slow-sample suffices. (2) never route the stick's +5V pin to an ADC pin; keep every signal <=3.3V (the 3V3-rail move handles this). (3) CALIBRATION: real pots don't sweep full-scale (~0.3-3.0V typical) -> firmware learns/observes per-axis min/max, applies center+deadzone, maps to 0-63. PLAYER 2: no ADC left after 1 stick (2 axes = both free channels); options: 74HC4051 8:1 analog mux (3 select GPIOs funnel all 4 axes through 1 ADC channel, sampled sequentially/frame) OR external I2C ADC e.g. ADS1115 4ch on I2C0 (SDA6/SCL7). summary: Implement USB hot-replug recovery: phantom-flood disconnect detection + PIO-USB re-enumeration
description: Implementation of the fix diagnosed in PIZERO-11b (child of it). On this rev3 board the disconnect is invisible to line_state/connected/ep_error/ints (the PIO SM pins the bus at J/FS); instead, an unplugged device makes PIO-USB flood ~180 byte-identical phantom HID reports/sec (HW-confirmed 2026-06-29). DESIGN: (1) DETECT -- in tuh_hid_report_received_cb (src/main.cpp), per (daddr,idx) track the previous report bytes + a consecutive-identical counter; when >=N identical reports arrive in a row (phantom flood; N~50-100, i.e. <~0.5s at 180/s), declare the device gone. A real boot keyboard sends reports only on key transitions, so it never trips; tune N against a real device held-key case (held key = repeated identical reports too -> may need 'identical AND rate>threshold', or exclude the held-key case by requiring the report to be the IDLE/all-zero report, since the phantom is the SM-held idle line). (2) RECOVER -- on detection, call pio_usb_host_stop() then pio_usb_host_restart() (both in pio_usb.h) to tear down + re-enumerate the root port so a freshly-attached or replugged device mounts cleanly; reset g_usb_devices / per-interface phantom counters. (3) SAFETY -- gate behind a flag (e.g. -DUSB_HOTPLUG_RECOVER); keep OFF the freeze-prone hot path (PIZERO-33); the stop/restart touches the shared PIO1 while libdvi runs on PIO0/core1 -- validate it does NOT wedge video/audio or trip the watchdog. PRE-WORK: add report-PAYLOAD logging to confirm phantom reports are byte-identical/idle (current diag build only COUNTS them). VERIFY ON HW: cold-boot keyboard works; unplug -> within ~1s a '[usb] re-enumerating' log + pio restart; replug (or attach a different device) -> [usb] device attached + usb=1 + rpts resumes on keypress; video stays 60fps, no freeze. ALTERNATIVES already RULED OUT by PIZERO-11b: E9-drain re-enable (line is driven, not leaking) and transfer-error detection (no errors fire). Parent PIZERO-11b. Roadmap: docs/ROADMAP.md.

summary: Firmware config/launcher overlay UI ("BIOS" menu over HDMI, function-key toggle)
description: No way to choose what to load without a rebuild/flash; media is fixed at build time (AUTORUN). Add a firmware-drawn overlay menu -- NOT emulated 6809 code -- that the port renders directly into the HDMI framebuffer, toggled by a function key (or a key held at boot). Scope: (1) input hook -- reserve a hotkey (e.g. F12 / Menu) in the HID path (src/main.cpp) that raises an overlay flag without reaching the guest; (2) render -- REUSE the real MC6847 alphanumeric renderer so the menu IS a native CoCo text screen (not a lookalike): render_alpha_frame() in coco_machine.cpp:924 already walks a 32x16 grid, pulls each glyph from the authentic font_6847t1[] char ROM into g_m.vdg_buffer, green-on-black, and flows through the existing coco_boot_blit_vdg_pizero() -> DVI path. Approach: REFACTOR render_alpha_frame(base) to accept a source pointer (const uint8_t *screen) instead of reading g_m.ram+base (~5-line change to the one chrow= line + expose it in the header) so the overlay owns a PRIVATE 512-byte screen-code buffer and never clobbers guest video RAM (the paused game's screen is preserved behind the menu). Alt (simpler, rejected): write into emulated text RAM 0x0400 and save/restore 512 bytes. SELECTION HIGHLIGHT is free: bit 6 of a screen code = inverse video (black-on-green, the iconic BASIC look) -- set it on the selected row's bytes, zero extra render code. Optional fancy border: bit 7 set -> SG4 2x2 semigraphics colour blocks. CONSTRAINTS (both authentic, lean in): uppercase-only 64-glyph set (ch&0x3F|0x40 -> @,A-Z,punct,0-9; no lowercase) needs a tiny ASCII->screen-code map; 32 cols x 16 rows grid (header + ~13-14 file entries + footer hint; long filenames truncate/scroll). Flow: fill menubuf (uppercase codes, bit6 on selected row) -> render_alpha_frame(menubuf) -> vdg_buffer -> existing pizero blit. COST is ~free: render ONCE per cursor change (not per frame) while emulation is paused, so the PIZERO-48 headroom concern does not apply -- a single alpha-frame render on each keypress. pause/freeze emulation while open; (3) SD browse -- list images on the microSD (SPI pins SCK30/MOSI31/MISO40/CS43, hw_config) filtered by type (cas/dsk/rom/cart); (4) actions -- load+mount selected image and (re)boot the machine; expose a few firmware-only settings the guest can't reach: SAM high-speed cap (see PIZERO-48), joystick source (USB gamepad vs header hat vs off, see PIZERO-50), audio env; (5) persist last selection/settings to SD or flash. Design the SD-listing + image-loader layer as a clean reusable module so a future in-emulator 'same-feel' CoCo-ROM launcher (v2, much larger lift) can reuse it. Gate the whole feature behind a build flag initially; validate it does not disturb 60Hz video / audio while open (emulation is paused, but the overlay composite runs on the same core-0 budget -- see PIZERO-48 headroom). Cross-link docs/ROADMAP.md. Depends on nothing hard; pairs naturally with SD work.

summary: GIME-style programmable palette for classic 6847 modes + BIOS editor + per-title .pal profiles
description: Non-traditional extension: give the classic MC6847 modes a CoCo3/GIME-style PROGRAMMABLE palette (real CoCo1/2 VDG colors were fixed -- this is impossible on original hw). The architecture is already 90% there: every renderer (render_alpha_frame/render_rg6_frame/render_graphics_frame in coco_machine.cpp) emits a 4-bit SEMANTIC palette index (PAL_GREEN..PAL_BRIGHT_ORANGE) into vdg_buffer, and the pizero blit does exactly one index->RGB lookup per pixel via g_vdg_rgb565_native[16] (coco_boot.cpp:488). That 16-entry LUT between VDG-index and output RGB IS the GIME palette-register architecture; it is just const today. PART 1 -- WRITABLE LUT + API: drop const on g_vdg_rgb565_native (already RAM-resident), add coco_set_palette_entry(idx,rgb) / get; keep a separate const MASTER copy for factory reset. Blit reads the LUT every frame so edits PREVIEW LIVE with zero repaint plumbing. No locking: LUT written by BIOS, read in blit; a torn read of one 16-bit entry mid-frame is cosmetically invisible for one frame. Only g_vdg_rgb565_native matters on this board (the byte-swapped g_vdg_rgb565 twin is dead AMOLED-path code). Current 12 named entries: 0 GREEN,1 YELLOW,2 BLUE(also RG6 artifact blue),3 RED,4 WHITE,5 CYAN,6 MAGENTA,7 ORANGE(also RG6 artifact orange),8 BLACK,9 DARK_GREEN,10 DARK_ORANGE,11 BRIGHT_ORANGE; 12-15 unused. NOTE indices are SEMANTIC so editing entry 0 recolors VDG green EVERYWHERE it appears (text ink, CG green, semigraphics, border) -- natural GIME behavior, intended; per-mode-independent palettes would need separate index spaces per mode = OUT OF SCOPE. Bonus: entries 2/7 double as RG6 NTSC-artifact colors so the same editor tunes the artifact red/blue tint (ties to PIZERO-43 phase work). PART 2 -- BIOS EDITOR (depends on PIZERO-53 overlay): pick an entry, adjust color, live-preview on whatever is on screen. Color depth: DEFAULT to CoCo3-authentic RGB222 (6-bit, 64-color GIME gamut) picker with an 'advanced/full-RGB565' toggle for 65k-color freedom. Render swatches as VDG semigraphics cells, inverse-video the selected one (reuse render_alpha_frame machinery from PIZERO-53). Actions: edit / reset-to-factory (copy master back) / save. PART 3 -- PER-TITLE .pal PROFILES: bind a saved 16-entry palette to a specific DSK/BIN/CAS/ROM so each game remembers its colors. Storage = SIDECAR file next to the image (SPACEWAR.DSK -> SPACEWAR.PAL), ~34 bytes: magic + version + 1-byte depth-mode flag + 16 entries stored as RGB222 (6-bit, output-depth-independent, survives future packing changes). Chose sidecar over a central manifest: matches the launcher's by-filename model, travels with the image on copy, no central corruption/dangling-entry risk. LOAD flow (hooks PIZERO-53 action step 4 load+mount): resolve palette in FALLBACK ORDER per-title <name>.pal -> user-global custom palette -> factory default; so untuned games look normal and tuned ones always come up right. SAVE flow: 'Save for this title' writes the sidecar keyed to the CURRENTLY-LOADED image path (launcher already tracks it for mount). EDGE CASES: built-in AUTORUN media has no path -> falls back to user-global (or reserve AUTORUN.PAL); image loaded outside the launcher -> no path -> global only. Persist the user-global custom palette too (PIZERO-53 persistence). PART 4 -- GUEST-SIDE GIME PALETTE (subsumes PIZERO-26, closed as superseded): beyond the BIOS editor, optionally let a RUNNING PROGRAM recolor live by intercepting guest writes to the real GIME palette addresses $FFB0-$FFBF on the CoCo bus (6-bit R-G-B, 2 bits/channel = 16 colors from 64) and routing them into the same writable LUT. This mirrors real CoCo3 VDG-compatible behavior -- a $FFB0+ recolor POKE program behaves the same here as on real hardware -- and stays fully TRANSPARENT: default LUT = stock CoCo colors, so unmodified games look normal until they poke the registers. Mirror the GIME addresses so CoCo-3-aware code just works; also optionally expose an extended RGB565 palette at our own addresses for beyond-hw color. WRINKLE (from PIZERO-26): PIZERO-15 precomputes glyph->packed-word LUTs with colors baked in (e.g. g_alpha_lut), so a palette write must REBUILD those small LUTs -- cheap, since palette writes are rare (once per screen, not per frame). TODO before coding Part 4: verify the exact GIME VDG-compatible default slot->color mapping against GIME docs rather than guessing. BOUNDARY: VDG+palette only, NOT full GIME/CoCo3 (no hi-res GIME bitmap modes, extra RAM/MMU, hw scroll, or GIME interrupts -- those remain PIZERO-16). Product context: docs/product-plan.md ('open platform you can extend' story). Gate behind a build flag. Depends on PIZERO-53 (overlay + SD + persistence); cross-link docs/ROADMAP.md. Verify on hw: edit green live in a running game; save; reboot/reload -> colors restored; a second game keeps its own; reset-to-factory works.

summary: Higher-fidelity NTSC artifact rendering (beyond the 2-bits->4-colors LUT)
description: FUTURE / fidelity enhancement. The current artifact path is a deliberate performance SHORTCUT, not composite decoding: render_rg6_frame (coco_machine.cpp:958) and its twin in vendored mc6847.c:52 map RG6/PMODE4 pixel PAIRS to one of four fixed palette entries (00->BLACK, 01->artifactA, 10->artifactB, 11->WHITE; A/B swapped by CSS + the compile-time phase flag). This nails the canonical 4-colour PMODE4 look that most artifact games rely on, but a real NTSC composite chain is an analog signal through finite chroma/luma bandwidth and produces things a context-free 2->4 LUT cannot: (1) MORE THAN 4 HUES -- specific multi-pixel patterns land at intermediate phase/amplitude and yield extra colours (greens/purples/half-luma shades demos + some games coax out); ours only ever emits black/A/B/white. (2) POSITION+NEIGHBOUR-DEPENDENT colour -- real hue depends on running phase and adjacent luma; ours decodes each pair in isolation, identically everywhere. (3) FRINGING / colour bleed / dot crawl at mono<->colour edges -- absent (hard-edged palette indices). (4) COVERAGE -- only RG6/GM7 artifacts; render_graphics_frame (other CG/RG modes) does straight fg/bg with NO artifacting, and the high-res 2-colour modes that also artifact on real hw are clean here. (5) fixed idealized PAL_BLUE/PAL_ORANGE swatches vs a real set's tint/temperature/power-on-phase drift (see PIZERO-43). WHY deferred: XRoar upstream HAS a phase-accurate composite renderer but this port dropped it; true composite sim is a per-pixel multi-tap filter -- expensive, and core-0 has only ~31% headroom at 1x (PIZERO-48). OPTIONS to close the gap, cheap->dear: (a) WIDER PATTERN LUT keyed on 3-4 pixels of context (precomputed) to fake the common extra hues without a real filter -- likely the best effort/quality tradeoff, still a table lookup in the hot blit; (b) extend artifacting to the other high-res mono modes; (c) a proper composite/NTSC decode pass (luma/chroma separation + bandpass) for full-gamut fidelity -- measure against the frame budget, likely needs core-1 headroom or a lower internal res. Pairs naturally with PIZERO-55 (both are 'what RGB does a given VDG pattern become'); a wider LUT could feed the same programmable-palette machinery. PRE-WORK: capture reference photos/captures of real-hardware artifacting for the target games to validate against. Not scheduled; log only. Cross-link docs/ROADMAP.md, PIZERO-43, PIZERO-55.

summary: Loadable/customizable VDG font from SD (.FNT + BIOS loader + per-title profiles)
description: Let the MC6847 alpha font be replaced from the SD card instead of being fixed at build time. Current font = const font_6847t1[1536] (128 glyphs x 12 rows, 8px wide, one byte/row MSB-first) in lib/xroar_core/src/mc6847/font-6847t1.c, placed in a .time_critical RAM section; the active renderer reads it at coco_machine.cpp:948. KEY: font loading is CLEANLY DECOUPLED from the PIZERO-55 palette work -- g_alpha_lut is indexed by the glyph ROW BYTE (0-255), not by character, so it bakes in COLORS not glyphs; a palette change rebuilds that LUT but a FONT change touches nothing but the font bytes. No LUT rebuild on font swap. PART 1 -- SWAPPABLE FONT + API: replace the direct font_6847t1[...] reference with an indirection g_font (default = the const ROM font); coco_load_font() fills a 1536-byte RAM buffer (keep it in .time_critical fast RAM so the hot render loop is unaffected -- 1.5KB is trivial on 520KB) and repoints g_font. ONLY render_alpha_frame (coco_machine.cpp:948) needs the change -- mc6847.c:427's per-scanline path is dead at runtime on this port. Keep the const font_6847t1 as the factory MASTER for reset-to-ROM (just repoint back). PART 2 -- FILE FORMAT: raw 8x12 bitmap, one byte/row MSB-first (same layout as the array); full 1536 bytes (128 glyphs) or just the 64-glyph alpha slot (768 bytes, the $40-$7F range). Small header (magic + version + width + height + glyph-count) so the loader VALIDATES: the renderer hard-assumes 8x12, so a font that isn't 8x12 must be REJECTED, not rendered garbled. Extension .FNT. PART 3 -- BIOS LOADER (depends on PIZERO-53 overlay): browse .FNT files on SD, load into the buffer, LIVE-PREVIEW (the menu itself redraws in the new font = instant feedback via the shared render_alpha_frame path), reset-to-ROM. PART 4 -- PER-TITLE SIDECAR: bind a font to a specific image, GAME.DSK -> GAME.FNT, mirroring PIZERO-55's .pal design exactly; FALLBACK ORDER per-title <name>.fnt -> user-global custom font -> factory ROM. So a game can carry BOTH its palette (.pal) and its font (.fnt). SAVE keyed to the currently-loaded image path (launcher tracks it). CONSTRAINT (state up front): alpha mode masks the screen code ch&0x3F|0x40, so it only ever indexes 64 GLYPHS ($40-$7F: @,A-Z,punct,0-9). A custom font REDEFINES those 64 (restyle/international-ish/game-matched look) but cannot ADD a 65th (no free lowercase) without changing the decode addressing -- note as a possible later extension, tie-in with the launcher lowercase discussion. EDGE CASES mirror PIZERO-55: AUTORUN/outside-launcher media has no path -> user-global font only. Persist the user-global font choice (PIZERO-53 persistence). Gate behind a build flag. Depends on PIZERO-53 (overlay + SD + persistence); sibling to PIZERO-55 (palette). Cross-link docs/ROADMAP.md. Verify on hw: load a .FNT, BASIC text redraws in the new glyphs; reset-to-ROM restores; a game's GAME.FNT auto-applies on load and a different game keeps its own.

summary: Bench: measure synth voice budget on real silicon (N dummy voices vs [run] telemetry)
description: PRE-WORK for PIZERO-17 (custom wavetable/sampled synth): validate the back-of-envelope cycles/voice + voice-count estimate on real RP2350 hardware BEFORE committing an engine architecture. Estimate to confirm: ~1100 cyc/sample total synth budget at ~3.5 ms/frame (of the ~5.3 ms core-0 headroom), giving ~4-5 Blofeld-grade voices (250 cyc/sample) up to ~10 simple voices (100 cyc/sample). METHOD: a flag-gated bench build (-DSYNTH_BENCH) that runs N dummy synth voices each frame in the core-0 audio path (audio_emit), generating into the SPSC ring (or a discard sink), and watches the existing [run] fps/cpu/render/blit serial telemetry (PIZERO-15). Sweep N upward until core-0 frame time approaches 16.67 ms / fps drops below 60, to find the real ceiling. VARIABLES to characterize: (1) per-voice complexity tiers -- (a) wavetable + linear interp + ADSR, (b) + resonant SVF filter + 2D wave morph, (c) full Blofeld-grade (morph + multimode filter + 2 env + 2 LFO); report cyc/sample for each. (2) FLOAT (M33 FPU) vs Q15 fixed-point (DSP MACs) inner loop -- measure both, pick the winner. (3) wavetable source: XIP-from-FLASH per-sample read vs SRAM-cached active-frame -- QUANTIFY the XIP cache-miss jitter that motivates the SRAM active-frame mirror, and the PCM pitched-playback (non-unity-rate flash walk) worst case. (4) RAM cost headroom -- SRAM is already ~89-94% used (PIZERO-18 audio + double-buffer video); report how much a realistic voice/wavetable-cache footprint adds and whether it fits. OUTPUT: a short docs note (or PIZERO-17 comment) with measured cyc/sample per tier, the safe max voice count at the 3-4 ms/frame budget, the float-vs-Q15 decision, and the flash/SRAM wavetable-access verdict -- these set PIZERO-17's configurable voice cap and memory model. Gate behind the bench flag; no product-env impact. Verify on hw: telemetry logs N, cyc/sample, and frame time; identify the N where fps first drops.

summary: Internal MIDI bus/router + CoCo bit-banger serial MIDI transport (firmware becomes Lyra's external UART box)
description: The CoCo-facing half of the MIDI subsystem. CORRECTED TRANSPORT (per user 2026-07-19): apps like Lyra do NOT use a cartridge ACIA -- they use the CoCo's built-in BIT-BANGER serial port (software-timed async serial toggled on a PIA1 line) feeding a CUSTOM EXTERNAL UART BOX (powered by +5V from the joystick port) that converts to MIDI DIN. EMULATION INSIGHT: the firmware simply BECOMES that external box -- tap the emulated bit-banger line, decode the async serial in firmware, forward as MIDI. No cartridge, no physical box, no joystick +5V needed (none of it is physical anymore) -> this is the zero-extra-hardware path. REUSES the cycle-accurate PIA-tap infrastructure from the audio work (PIZERO-18 already samples PIA1 PORT A at emulation-tick resolution; the DAC tap is the template). TRANSPORT: (1) OUT (CoCo->MIDI) -- tap the RS-232 serial-out bit (CoCo bit-banger, believed PIA1 PA1 / $FF20 bit 1, CONFIRM via PIZERO-61), watch its transitions over emulated cycles, software-UART-decode async frames at Lyra's baud into MIDI bytes, push to the router. (2) IN (MIDI->CoCo) -- synthesize the async serial waveform on the serial-in line (believed PIA1 PB0 / $FF22 bit 0, CONFIRM via PIZERO-61) with cycle-accurate bit timing so Lyra's software-UART-receive reads incoming MIDI. ROUTER: an internal software MIDI bus carrying parsed events (handle running status, SysEx, MIDI clock); ANY source -> ANY sink, configurable. SOURCES: the bit-banger transport (guest), external endpoints (PIZERO-60). SINKS: the synth (PIZERO-17), external endpoints (PIZERO-60), the bit-banger IN (back to guest). So Lyra can play the internal synth AND drive real gear simultaneously; a DAW/controller can drive the synth OR feed Lyra. COCO2 UNTOUCHED: the serial tap/inject only runs when MIDI is ENABLED (config toggle); no bus/tap cost otherwise; router runs only on traffic; buffers are a few hundred bytes. Build-flag gated, off in the product env. NOTE (real-hardware only): Lyra's box occupied the joystick port for +5V, so a purist using REAL Lyra hardware would conflict with the PIZERO-50 joystick hat -- irrelevant to the all-emulated path (joystick port stays free). DEPENDS ON: PIZERO-61 (Lyra serial params: PIA bits, baud, framing, whether Lyra bit-bangs 31250 directly or the box reclocks) to set the decoder; PIZERO-17 for the synth sink (but testable EARLY by routing to a PIZERO-60 USB-MIDI endpoint before the synth exists). Cross-link docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/hdmi-audio-notes.md (shared PIA-tap technique), PIZERO-60. Verify on hw: run Lyra, notes reach the internal synth / USB-MIDI out at correct pitch+timing; external MIDI in reaches Lyra; plain CoCo2 boot unaffected with MIDI off.

summary: External MIDI I/O endpoints (USB-MIDI device + host; optional DIN-5)
description: The outside-world half of the MIDI subsystem: physical/virtual endpoints that plug into the PIZERO-59 router. Three endpoints, only one needs added hardware. (1) USB-MIDI DEVICE via NATIVE USB -- NO EXTRA HARDWARE. This board's native RP2350 USB is already a DEVICE (it runs the CDC serial console + WAV dump). Add a MIDI interface to the existing TinyUSB/Adafruit_TinyUSB COMPOSITE descriptor (CDC + MIDI) so the board appears to a PC/DAW as a class-compliant MIDI port over the cable that's ALREADY plugged in. This is the marquee 'external integration without additional hardware' path: Lyra -> PIZERO-59 router -> USB-MIDI -> DAW/hardware synth, and back. Use Adafruit_USBD_MIDI; verify it composes with the existing CDC (do not break the serial console/telemetry). (2) USB-MIDI HOST via PIO-USB -- NO EXTRA HARDWARE beyond the class-compliant controller itself. Enumerate a USB-MIDI keyboard/controller on the PIO host port (GPIO28/29); pairs with the hub (PIZERO-54) so a keyboard + a MIDI controller coexist. Needs TinyUSB MIDI-host class support on the Pico-PIO-USB stack (verify availability; may need a report/class handler like the HID path). (3) DIN-5 SERIAL MIDI -- THE ONLY option needing hardware: a UART on a free GPIO + standard MIDI circuit (optocoupler 6N138 input / current-loop output, DIN jacks). Optional, for vintage gear. All three are build-flag gated and cost nothing when inactive (USB polling only when an endpoint is present) -> CoCo2 path untouched. DEPENDS ON: PIZERO-59 (router). Composes with PIZERO-54 (hub) for the host path. Cross-link docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/BUILD.md (new flags). Verify on hw: (1) board enumerates as a USB-MIDI device on a PC and passes notes both ways while CDC still works; (2) a USB-MIDI controller on the host port drives the synth; (3) [if built] DIN in/out with real gear.

summary: Pre-work: reverse-engineer Lyra's bit-banged serial MIDI driver (params for PIZERO-59)
description: PRE-WORK / RESEARCH that GATES PIZERO-59's serial transport. User-confirmed mechanism (2026-07-19): Lyra drives the CoCo's built-in BIT-BANGER RS-232 serial port into a CUSTOM EXTERNAL UART BOX powered by +5V from the joystick port, which converts to MIDI DIN. To make the firmware faithfully BECOME that box, nail the exact parameters the emulated transport must match: (1) which PIA line carries serial OUT and which carries serial IN (believed PIA1 PA1 / $FF20 bit 1 out, PIA1 PB0 / $FF22 bit 0 in -- CONFIRM, do not guess); (2) the BAUD rate Lyra bit-bangs at, and the frame format (start/data/stop bits, parity); (3) CRITICAL: does Lyra bit-bang at MIDI rate (31250) DIRECTLY -- so the box just level-shifts and our firmware forwards bytes 1:1 -- or does it send at some other CoCo-friendly rate that the box's UART RECLOCKS to 31250 (so our firmware must decode at rate X and re-emit as MIDI)? This determines the decoder clock. (4) any handshake/flow-control lines the box used; (5) whether Lyra relies on interrupt or tight-loop bit timing (affects how cycle-accurate our tap must be -- likely very, like the audio DAC tap). METHOD: use the analyze-rom and trace-calls skills on Lyra's binary/driver to find the bit-bang routine and extract the timing constants + PIA addresses; cross-check against XRoar's serial handling and published CoCo bit-banger docs. Also document the external box's behavior for the record (and for anyone building real hardware, incl. the joystick-port +5V tap that conflicts with the PIZERO-50 joystick hat on real hardware only). OUTPUT: a short transport spec (PIA bits + baud + framing + reclock-or-not) that PIZERO-59 implements against. Cross-link PIZERO-59, PIZERO-60.

summary: GIME-compatible programmable timer + minimal interrupt registers (partial GIME; runs SOME unmodified CoCo3 timer software)
description: Add a CoCo3/GIME-COMPATIBLE programmable interrupt timer so SOME unmodified CoCo3 software runs on this CoCo2 base -- without full GIME and without compromising CoCo2 (user goal 2026-07-19: a compatible LAYOUT, not our own ad-hoc device). CURRENT MODEL (recap): 6809 IRQ <- PIA0 (HS/FS sync, coco_machine.cpp:481), FIRQ <- PIA1 (CART line, :482); rates are FIXED. The scheduled-countdown needed for a timer ALREADY EXISTS as cart_toggle_remaining (:806-811) -- a cycles-to-next-pulse counter; the timer generalizes it to a register-loaded interval (no per-cycle hot-loop cost, fires only when it fires). IMPLEMENT (authentic GIME register layout, all in the $FF90-$FF95 block -- UNUSED on a CoCo2 so decoding is safe): (1) TIMER reload $FF94 (MSB, bits 11-8) / $FF95 (LSB) = 12-bit down-counter; on underflow raise the interrupt + auto-reload. (2) CLOCK SOURCE via INIT1 $FF91 TINS bit: fast 3.579545 MHz (~279 ns, = 4x the 0.895 MHz 6809 clock -> interval_cycles = reload*... convert) vs horizontal 15.734 kHz (~63.5 us); both convert cheaply to 6809-cycle intervals for the scheduler. (3) MINIMAL INTERRUPT CONTROLLER: $FF92 (IRQ enable) / $FF93 (FIRQ enable) with at least the TIMER source bit; read-to-clear status; route the timer to IRQ or FIRQ per the enable regs (OR into the existing MC6809_IRQ_SET/FIRQ_SET). Decode INIT0 $FF90 / INIT1 $FF91 as needed. (4) RELOAD QUIRK: match GIME period behavior (period = reload + 1 on the 1986 GIME, + 2 on the 1987 -- CONFIRM exact; matters for pitch-accurate music); pick a rev or make it a build option -- research item. COMPATIBILITY BOUNDARY (the honest 'some'): RUNS CoCo3 programs that (a) stay in CoCo2/VDG-compatible video, (b) install their OWN IRQ/FIRQ handler (we boot CoCo2 Extended Color BASIC, whose interrupt handler is PIA-based NOT GIME-aware, so ROM-handler-dependent GIME interrupt use won't work), (c) don't need the MMU / 512K / GIME hi-res modes, (d) don't hard-gate on full-GIME detection. SWEET SPOT = interrupt-driven MUSIC / timing / demo routines that just want a fast programmable tick. WON'T RUN: anything using GIME hi-res video, the MMU, 512K RAM, or the Super ECB ROM handlers. TIES to the music work: this is the guest-side programmable tick for a MIDI clock / sequencer / synth-envelope updates (PIZERO-17 synth, PIZERO-59 MIDI). HOST COST is proportional to fire rate; add a sanity FLOOR on the interval so a pathologically fast timer can't blow the ~5.3 ms core-0 headroom (PIZERO-48). Build-flag GATED; zero cost to a plain CoCo2 boot when off (only joins the IRQ/FIRQ OR when enabled). ALTERNATIVES: (B) our own non-GIME address block for the timer = simpler but runs ZERO existing CoCo3 software -> REJECTED in favor of the compatible layout per the goal; (C) FULL GIME (MMU, hi-res video, all interrupt sources, 512K) = OUT OF SCOPE, large lift and directly breaks CoCo2 purity. PRE-WORK: pick 2-3 candidate CoCo3 timer/music programs (VDG-mode, own-handler) to validate against; confirm the reload-quirk rev to emulate. VERIFY on hw: a candidate CoCo3 music/timer program runs unmodified at correct tempo; plain CoCo2 boot byte-identical with the timer disabled. Cross-link docs/ROADMAP.md, PIZERO-17, PIZERO-59.
