summary: SD write foundation: writable file layer, flush/sync policy + write-latency measurement
description: FOUNDATION for all SD write work (blocks PIZERO-65/66/67/69). VERIFIED CURRENT STATE: the port is entirely read-only in OUR code -- every f_open is FA_READ (coco_boot.cpp:100 ROM, :276 autorun.txt, :324 DSK attach, :379 LOADM .bin) and there are ZERO occurrences of f_write/f_sync/f_unlink/f_mkdir in src/ or lib/. Nothing below us blocks writing: the carlk3 no-OS-FatFS stack is configured write-capable (FF_FS_READONLY=0, FF_USE_MKFS=1, FF_FS_EXFAT=1, FF_USE_LFN=3) with disk_write()/sd_write_blocks() implemented in sd_card_spi.c and get_fattime() supplied by the lib's my_rtc.c. So this is purely additive firmware work. IMPLEMENT: (1) a small writable-file helper layer next to the existing coco_boot read helpers -- open-for-write/create, write, sync, close, atomic-replace (write to .TMP then f_rename over the target) so an interrupted write never truncates a good file; (2) an explicit FLUSH/SYNC POLICY -- decide and document when f_sync is called (per sector? per DECB command completion? on an idle timer? on BIOS exit?), since FatFs buffers FAT+dir updates and a power cut between the data write and the FAT update corrupts the image; (3) MEASURE REAL WRITE LATENCY -- instrument single-sector (256B), full-block (512B) and multi-block writes, plus the f_sync cost, and record worst-case against the 16.67 ms frame budget. This measurement is the whole input to PIZERO-65: per PIZERO-48 core 0 has only ~31% slack at 1x, and SD block-erase stalls are known to run tens-to-hundreds of ms, so a synchronous write on the emulation thread is expected to break audio/video. ALSO NOTE: hw_config.c wires no card-detect/write-protect pin (grep: no cd_gpio/use_card_detect), so a card pulled mid-write is currently unguarded -- decide whether to wire CD (GPIO22 per the vendor demo) or accept the risk and document it. get_fattime() with no RTC will stamp a fixed epoch, so written files get bogus dates -- acceptable, but note it in docs. ACCEPTANCE: a firmware-written test file appears on the card with correct contents after a clean power cycle, and the measured worst-case write+sync latency is written into this ticket and docs/ (it decides PIZERO-65's design).

summary: Deferred sector write-back: keep SD writes off the emulation hot path
description: The hard part of the SD-write workstream, deliberately kept SEPARATE from PIZERO-66 so the timing risk can't be buried inside the feature ticket (user decision 2026-08-05). PROBLEM: a synchronous f_write inside the FDC Write Sector handler will blow the frame budget. Per PIZERO-48 the pacing model leaves core 0 only ~31% slack at 1x (~9.4 ms used of the 16.67 ms/frame), while an SD write can stall tens-to-hundreds of ms on block erase -- one guest SAVE would starve the core-1 audio ring (underrun/warble, the class of bug PIZERO-35/38/39 just fixed) and drop video frames. So the emulated FDC must ACK a write quickly and the physical write must happen elsewhere. IMPLEMENT: a write-back queue between the FDC and the SD -- guest Write Sector copies the 256 B into a queued dirty-sector entry, sets FDC status complete, and returns immediately; a drainer performs the real f_write/f_sync outside the emulation hot path. DESIGN DECISIONS to settle with measurements from PIZERO-64: (a) WHERE the drainer runs -- core 0 in the idle slack after the frame's emulation completes (simplest, bounded by measured slack) vs core 1 (already owns libdvi scanout + the audio ring; adding SD SPI there risks the video path) vs draining only during guest idle. Default recommendation: core 0, post-frame, with a per-frame byte budget so one drain never exceeds the remaining slack. (b) QUEUE DEPTH and what happens when it's full -- DECB writes a whole granule in a burst, so size for that; on overflow either stall the guest (honest, brief) or return an FDC error. (c) COALESCING adjacent dirty sectors into one multi-block write. (d) SD SPI BUS OWNERSHIP -- the existing read path (coco_boot_disk_read_sector, called synchronously from the FDC) shares the bus with the drainer, so a read must not interleave mid-write; also a read of a still-queued dirty sector must see the QUEUED data, not the stale on-card bytes. (e) DURABILITY WINDOW -- a queued-but-unwritten sector is lost on power cut; bound it (flush within N frames) and force a full flush on BIOS entry/exit and before any reset. ACCEPTANCE on HW: a guest SAVE of a sizeable program completes with NO audible audio glitch and NO dropped frames (watch the [run] telemetry: core-0 frame time stays < 16.76 ms throughout), the data is correct after power-cycle, and the queue never overflows silently -- overflow is logged. Depends on PIZERO-64 (its latency numbers are this ticket's design input). Blocks PIZERO-66.

summary: FDC Write Sector -> guest SAVE/SAVEM to .DSK on SD
description: The headline feature: let a program running on the emulated CoCo write to its disk image. KEY INSIGHT (verified): SAVE and SAVEM are NOT XRoar-side commands -- they are Disk BASIC (DECB) commands implemented in 6809 code in the disk11.rom cart running INSIDE the guest. DECB does its own directory and granule/FAT allocation in software; all it needs from the hardware is a working Write Sector. So this one change unlocks SAVE, SAVEM, KILL, COPY, RENAME and BACKUP largely for free. CURRENT STUB: lib/coco_machine/src/coco_machine.cpp:252-257 handles WD279x Type II Write Sector (command top nibble 0xA/0xB) by setting fdc_status = 0x40 -- bit 6 = WRITE PROTECT -- and completing cleanly. That is an honest 'this disk is write-protected' answer, not a crash, and it is exactly the hook point. Correspondingly coco_machine_install_disk_reader() (coco_machine.cpp:307) installs only a READER (coco_disk_read_sector_fn), and coco_boot_disk_read_sector (coco_boot.cpp:336) has no write counterpart. IMPLEMENT: (1) mirror the reader API -- coco_disk_write_sector_fn + coco_machine_install_disk_writer(), and coco_boot_disk_write_sector(drive,track,sector,const uint8_t[256]) in coco_boot.cpp; (2) replace the 0x40 stub with a real Type II write: assert DRQ, accept 256 bytes written to $FF4B into fdc_buf (the inverse of the existing fdc_io_read drain at :270-282), then hand the full sector to the writer callback and fire INTRQ/NMI the same way the read path does at completion; (3) reopen the attached image writable -- coco_boot_attach_dsk currently opens FA_READ only (coco_boot.cpp:324) and holds it in g_dsk_file, so it needs FA_READ|FA_WRITE with a graceful fallback to read-only (i.e. keep returning 0x40, a genuine write-protect answer) when the file can't be opened writable or the card is absent; (4) route the actual write through the PIZERO-65 write-back queue, NOT a direct synchronous f_write; (5) honour the existing geometry guards (track<=34, sector 1-18, drive 0 only -- see :341-348) and return proper FDC error status rather than silently dropping out-of-range writes. ACCEPTANCE on HW: in Disk BASIC, SAVE of a BASIC program then NEW then LOAD round-trips it; SAVEM of a machine-language block round-trips via LOADM; DIR shows the new file with a plausible size; the change survives a power cycle and the .DSK is still mountable in desktop xroar with the saved file intact. Depends on PIZERO-64 and PIZERO-65. [RE-SCOPED 2026-08-05: floppy support is now PERIPHERAL support, not the route to writable storage -- see PIZERO-79 and the PIZERO-70..74 filesystem layer, which is the supported way to create and edit files. This ticket survives as legacy polish for running/writing old .DSK images and is no longer on the critical path; demoted high -> low.]

summary: Firmware-side SD persistence API (config + .pal/.fnt sidecars) -- undeclared dependency of PIZERO-53/55/57
description: Distinct from guest-side disk writes (PIZERO-66): this is the FIRMWARE writing its own files to the card -- the BIOS config blob and the per-title sidecars. ROADMAP GAP found 2026-08-05: PIZERO-53 (BIOS overlay: 'firmware-only settings', persistence), PIZERO-55 (palette editor -- 'save flow: save for this title writes the sidecar keyed to the currently-loaded image path', per-title .PAL) and PIZERO-57 (loadable VDG font -- per-title .FNT sidecars, 'save keyed to the currently-loaded image path') ALL assume the firmware can write to SD, and NONE of them declares that dependency -- while the port is in fact read-only (see PIZERO-64). This ticket makes the capability explicit and shared so the three UX tickets don't each grow their own half-baked writer. IMPLEMENT: (1) a small typed settings store -- read/modify/write a firmware config file (e.g. /coco/config.txt or a versioned binary blob) with a schema version field and forward-compatible defaults, so an older firmware meeting a newer file degrades instead of corrupting; (2) sidecar write/read helpers keyed to the currently-loaded image path (GAME.DSK -> GAME.PAL / GAME.FNT), matching the per-title -> user-global -> factory fallback chain those tickets already specify; (3) atomic replace (write .TMP + f_rename, from PIZERO-64) so an interrupted save never leaves a truncated palette/font/config that bricks the next boot -- the fallback chain must also treat a malformed sidecar as absent; (4) explicit flush on BIOS exit. NOTE this path is much easier than PIZERO-66 on timing: BIOS saves happen while the overlay is up and the user is interacting, not inside the emulation hot loop, so a synchronous write+sync is acceptable here (a brief hitch during a menu save is fine) -- it does NOT need the PIZERO-65 queue. Depends on PIZERO-64 only. Should land before or alongside PIZERO-53 so the overlay has somewhere to persist to; unblocks the save half of PIZERO-55 and PIZERO-57.

summary: DECB disk maintenance: DSKINI/format, multi-drive, write-protect toggle, proper FDC error status
description: Completes the guest-side disk story once PIZERO-66 can write single sectors. Turns 'SAVE works' into 'the disk subsystem behaves like a disk subsystem'. IMPLEMENT: (1) DSKINI (format) -- DECB's formatter issues WD279x Type III Write Track, currently a blanket stub (coco_machine.cpp:259-262 sets fdc_status=0x10 RNF for all Type III). Either implement enough Write Track to satisfy DECB, or (simpler and probably better) intercept format and synthesise a fresh 161280-byte JVC image with an initialised DECB directory/granule map -- which also gives the BIOS a 'create new blank disk' action. (2) MULTI-DRIVE -- coco_boot_disk_read_sector hard-rejects drive != 0 (coco_boot.cpp:340) though the FDC already decodes the one-hot drive select from the $FF40 latch into fdc_drive (:295-297); extend to an array of attached images so drive 0/1 both mount (needed for COPY and BACKUP between two disks, and for a data disk alongside a game). (3) GEOMETRY beyond 35x18x1 -- the read path hardcodes 35 tracks / 18 sectors / single-sided (:318, :341); accept 40/80-track and double-sided images by deriving geometry from file size at attach time. (4) WRITE-PROTECT as a real, user-visible state -- a BIOS per-drive WP toggle (and automatic WP when the file can't be opened writable), reported through the existing 0x40 status bit; protects a pristine game image from an accidental SAVE. (5) HONEST ERROR STATUS -- map disk-full, I/O failure, card-absent and out-of-range onto the right WD279x status bits (RNF 0x10, write fault, write protect 0x40) so DECB prints a sensible error instead of hanging or silently succeeding; a queue overflow from PIZERO-65 also needs a status mapping here. ACCEPTANCE on HW: DSKINI produces a disk that DIR reports empty and that accepts a SAVE; BACKUP/COPY between drive 0 and 1 works; WP-toggling a disk makes SAVE fail with a write-protect error and leaves the image byte-identical; filling a disk yields a clean DECB error, not a hang. Depends on PIZERO-66. [RE-SCOPED 2026-08-05: legacy peripheral polish only -- DECB's format/granule/multi-drive model is explicitly not the future storage model. See PIZERO-79; demoted medium -> low.]

summary: Emulator save-states: wire XRoar's serialise.c fs_* stubs to FatFs (freeze/restore whole machine)
description: Whole-machine snapshot to SD -- freeze the emulated CoCo mid-game and restore it later. Independent of the disk-write chain (PIZERO-66/68): different mechanism, different feature. FOUND 2026-08-05: the infrastructure is ALREADY VENDORED AND COMPILED IN -- lib/xroar_core/src/serialise.c is 846 lines of real XRoar snapshot machinery (and part.c/part.h provide the part-tree walk it serialises over). What blocks it is purely the I/O primitives: lib/xroar_core/src/xroar_stubs.c:21-45 no-ops EVERY fs_* function it depends on, under the explicit comment 'serialise.c references these for save-state I/O; we don't implement save-state on the Pico, so every stub is a no-op'. That is ~18 one-line functions (fs_write_uint8/16/16_le/31, fs_read_uint8/16/16_le/31, fs_write_vuint32/vint32, fs_read_vuint32/vint32, fs_sizeof_vuint32/vint32, fs_file_size, fs_truncate, fs_file_crc32, fs_file_crc32_block) all currently returning -1/0. IMPLEMENT: (1) a FILE* -> FatFs FIL bridge -- lib/xroar_core/src/fs.h is written against stdio (FILE*, off_t, ftruncate semantics), so either provide a tiny shim type or adapt fs.h; note fs_truncate must leave the file position at the new EOF per its documented contract, and fs_file_crc32 must record and restore position; (2) implement the fs_* primitives over that bridge; (3) decide WHAT is in a snapshot for this port -- serialise.c walks the part tree, so confirm the parts we actually instantiate (RAM, mc6809, mc6883 SAM, both mc6821 PIAs, mc6847 VDG) round-trip, and decide how the NON-xroar firmware state is handled: the attached DSK path, any PIZERO-65 dirty-sector queue (MUST be flushed before snapshotting, else the restored state disagrees with the image on the card), the audio ring, and the VDG palette/font if PIZERO-55/57 have landed; (4) version the snapshot format and reject mismatches rather than restoring garbage; (5) surface save/load slots in the BIOS overlay (PIZERO-53). SIZE CHECK before committing to this: 64 KB RAM + CPU/PIA/SAM/VDG state is a ~64-70 KB file -- trivial for the card, but the serialisation buffer must not blow the SRAM budget (README notes SRAM is ~89-94% full), so stream straight to FatFs rather than building an image in RAM. ACCEPTANCE on HW: freeze a running game, power-cycle, restore, and it resumes correctly with sound and video intact. Depends on PIZERO-64; snapshot-vs-disk consistency depends on PIZERO-65 if that has landed; BIOS slots depend on PIZERO-53.

summary: Storage backend abstraction: one device interface, SD/FatFs as the first backend
description: Layer 0 of the DECB-replacement stack (user direction 2026-08-05: floppies and their data structures are obsolete; we already have a fast hierarchical filesystem with long names, and pretending it is a floppy wastes it). Define ONE backend interface that the VFS (PIZERO-71) sits on, so storage can be SD, RAM, USB mass storage, DriveWire or a FujiNet-class network device without the guest or the command surface changing. SCOPE: the interface itself (mount/unmount, identify/capabilities, read/write/flush, error model) plus SD/FatFs as backend #1 by wrapping the existing coco_boot read helpers and the PIZERO-64 write layer. Capabilities must be queryable, not assumed -- read-only vs writable, seekable, max path/name length, whether hierarchy is supported -- because DriveWire and RAM disk differ sharply from FatFs. Keep it a C interface with no 6809 knowledge. Depends on PIZERO-64 for the write path. Blocks PIZERO-71.

summary: VFS core: hierarchy, long filenames, create/write/edit/delete/rename, directory enumeration
description: Layer 1: the filesystem semantics the guest actually gets, replacing DECB's flat 8.3-uppercase 68-granule model. PRIMARY FOCUS per user direction is the WRITE side -- creating, extending and editing newly generated files is the point of the exercise, not just loading. SCOPE: path handling (hierarchical, long names -- FatFs is already built with FF_USE_LFN 3), open/close/read/write/seek/truncate, create/delete/rename/mkdir, directory enumeration, and file attributes/size/timestamps (note: no RTC, so get_fattime stamps a fixed epoch -- see PIZERO-64). Defines the canonical error codes that the hypercall ABI (PIZERO-72) surfaces to the guest. Runs entirely in C over the PIZERO-70 backend interface; no 6809 code here. Depends on PIZERO-70. Blocks PIZERO-72.

summary: Guest hypercall ABI: versioned command-block protocol for filesystem access (the contract)
description: Layer 2 and the CRUX of the whole design: the stable contract between guest code and the firmware filesystem. Everything else can be rewritten; this cannot, because BASIC (PIZERO-74), Bare Naked Forth and any future guest software all bind to it. Get it right before building on it. SCOPE: claim an unused I/O address range (the $FF90-$FF93 area is contested by PIZERO-62's GIME timer -- pick deliberately and document), define a command block laid out in guest RAM (opcode, handle, long-path pointer, buffer pointer, length, result/errno), and the doorbell/completion signalling. MUST BE VERSIONED from day one -- a capability/version query opcode so guest code can detect what it is talking to and degrade instead of corrupting. MUST HANDLE LATENCY: an SD write can stall tens-to-hundreds of ms while core 0 has only ~31% slack per frame (PIZERO-48), so the ABI needs either explicit async (submit, poll status, complete) or a documented blocking contract with the PIZERO-65 write-back queue behind it -- decide this HERE, since retrofitting async into a synchronous ABI breaks every client. Uses the same bus-interception technique as PIZERO-55's palette registers. Document the ABI in docs/ as a first-class spec, not a code comment. Depends on PIZERO-71 (semantics) and PIZERO-65 (latency strategy). Blocks PIZERO-73/74.

summary: Replacement cart ROM: thin 6809 shim over the hypercall + 6809 assembler in the build
description: Layer 3a: the guest-side code that replaces disk11.rom in the $C000 cart slot. DESIGN RULE: keep it THIN. All filesystem logic lives in C on the RP2350 behind the PIZERO-72 hypercall; the ROM is a shim that marshals arguments and hooks BASIC. This is what makes the backend abstraction possible and keeps us out of a full DOS-in-assembly project. SCOPE: an 8 KB cart image, the BASIC hook points needed by PIZERO-74, and the marshalling glue. NEW BUILD DEPENDENCY: this needs a 6809 assembler (lwasm or asm6809) wired into the PlatformIO build, with the assembled ROM embedded in flash -- document it in docs/BUILD.md, which is the source of truth for the build. Note the port already loads carts by name (coco_boot_load_cart_named, coco_boot.h:49) so the mounting path exists. Depends on PIZERO-72.

summary: New guest command surface: filesystem commands replacing DECB's
description: Layer 3b: what the user actually types. Replaces DECB's command set with commands built for a hierarchical long-filename filesystem instead of a 35-track floppy -- explicitly NOT DECB-compatible (user direction: provide the abilities without the arcane DECB context and its limitations). SCOPE: load/save of programs and binaries, directory listing with hierarchy, change/make/remove directory, delete/rename/copy, and sequential file I/O for guest programs (the equivalent of OPEN/CLOSE/PRINT#/INPUT# but over real paths). Decide and document the naming: reusing DECB keywords with new semantics is friendlier but silently changes behaviour for old software, while new keywords are honest but unfamiliar -- pick one and record the rationale. Error messages should surface the PIZERO-71 error codes usefully rather than DECB's numbered errors. Depends on PIZERO-72 and PIZERO-73. Bare Naked Forth binds to PIZERO-72 directly and does not need this ticket.

summary: RAM disk backend (fast VFS test target, no card required)
description: A backend with no hardware and no latency, useful out of proportion to its size: it lets the VFS (PIZERO-71), hypercall (PIZERO-72) and command surface (PIZERO-74) be developed and tested without an SD card inserted and without the write-latency problem confounding results -- and it is a real user feature (scratch space, fast intermediate files). SCOPE: a small backend over an SRAM allocation, sized against the tight budget (README: SRAM ~89-94% full, PSRAM unpopulated), so expect tens of KB, not megabytes; size configurable, contents volatile, capabilities reported honestly via the PIZERO-70 interface. Depends on PIZERO-70.

summary: DriveWire / serial storage backend
description: Backend over a simple serial transport -- host-provided storage with no local media, and the on-ramp to FujiNet-class networked storage (PIZERO-77), which the user flags as a major focus. SCOPE: the transport plus enough of the protocol to serve the PIZERO-70 backend interface. NOTE the framing question up front: DriveWire is natively a virtual-FLOPPY protocol (sector reads/writes against disk images on the host), which sits oddly under a hierarchy-and-long-names VFS -- so decide whether we speak stock DriveWire (compatible with existing host servers, but constrained to its sector model) or a file-level protocol over the same wire (better fit, needs our own host tool). Record the decision and rationale. Serial plumbing overlaps the bit-banger tap technique from PIZERO-59; check whether the transport can be shared. Depends on PIZERO-70.

summary: FujiNet-class networked storage over TCP/IP hardware
description: Networked storage and services in the FujiNet mould, with appropriate TCP/IP-capable hardware attached -- flagged by the user as a major focus, ticketed now to hold the shape rather than to start. SCOPE (to be narrowed): which hardware provides the network stack (the RP2350 has no radio; an ESP32-class companion or a wired module on a spare header is the likely route -- this is a hardware decision, so it needs the schematic and a free-pin audit before design), then a backend over it serving the PIZERO-70 interface, and which FujiNet-style services beyond file access are in scope. Deliberately shallow until PIZERO-70/71/72 are real and the hardware path is chosen. Depends on PIZERO-70 and PIZERO-76's transport work.

summary: USB mass-storage backend
description: Backend for a USB drive on the PIO-USB host port. SCOPE: USB MSC class support plus a PIZERO-70 backend over it. CONSTRAINTS to check first: PIO-USB already costs real core budget and the host stack currently runs one device on the root port, so using a drive alongside the keyboard needs the hub work (PIZERO-54); MSC bulk transfers plus DVI scanout plus emulation on the same chip is a genuine throughput question, so measure before designing. Lower priority than the SD and RAM backends since SD already serves the primary use case. Depends on PIZERO-70 and PIZERO-54.

summary: Demote floppy support to a peripheral: DECB/.DSK as optional legacy device
description: Formalises the reframing (user direction 2026-08-05): floppy emulation stops being the storage model and becomes ordinary peripheral support, for people who want to run old images. The new filesystem layer (PIZERO-70..74) is the DEFAULT; DECB and the emulated WD279x become an opt-in device. SCOPE: (1) boot policy -- the replacement cart ROM (PIZERO-73) loads by default instead of disk11.rom, with DECB + a .DSK selectable per-title via autorun.txt and the BIOS overlay (PIZERO-53); the two models must not both claim the cart slot, so make the choice explicit and documented. (2) COEXISTENCE: the existing direct-load path (autorun.txt direct_name -> coco_boot_parse_loadm, main.cpp:1084) and the .DSK path (:1097) are already mutually exclusive at boot -- fold both into one coherent 'what am I booting' decision alongside the new default. (3) Re-scope the legacy tickets: guest SAVE/SAVEM to .DSK (PIZERO-66) and DECB disk maintenance (PIZERO-68) are now nice-to-have peripheral polish, not the path to writable storage -- that is PIZERO-71's job. (4) Documentation: README/ROADMAP must say plainly that floppy compatibility is peripheral support and the new VFS is the supported way to create and edit files, so the intent is not re-litigated later. Depends on PIZERO-73 for the default cart; touches PIZERO-53.

summary: Evaluate 4-bit PIO SDIO vs 1-bit SPI for SD (throughput + the only non-blocking transfer API we have)
description:
Evaluate switching the SD backend from 1-bit SPI to 4-bit PIO SDIO. Two independent payoffs: raw throughput, and -- the reason this is ticketed separately -- it is the ONLY path in our stack with a non-blocking, start/poll transfer API.

FINDINGS (verified in the installed lib, 2026-08-05, carlk3 no-OS-FatFS-SD-SDIO-SPI-RPi-Pico 3.5.1): (1) NOTHING in the PlatformIO/Arduino ecosystem offers an async FILESYSTEM. Every FatFs entry point in ff15/source/ff.h is a synchronous FRESULT f_xxx() (f_forward takes a callback but is a read-side pull helper, not asynchrony). SdFat (installed as an Adafruit SPIFlash dep) is likewise synchronous. So no library choice removes PIZERO-65. (2) The carlk3 driver DOES use DMA (sd_driver/SPI/my_spi.c, sd_driver/dma_interrupts.c, sd_driver/SDIO/rp2040_sdio.c) but then SPIN-WAITS on it -- my_spi.c:198 'while (dma_channel_is_busy(rx) || dma_channel_is_busy(tx)) tight_loop_contents();' and rp2040_sdio.c:250 -- so DMA buys throughput, not free CPU; from core 0 it is fully blocking. (3) A vestigial async hook exists but is DEAD: sd_callback_t / azplatform_set_sd_callback (sd_driver/SDIO/ZuluSCSI_platform.h:75-76), inherited from ZuluSCSI, is declared and never defined or called anywhere in the library -- do not build on it. (4) THE ASYNC-SHAPED API IS IN THE SDIO BACKEND: rp2040_sdio.h:101-111 exposes rp2040_sdio_tx_start()/tx_poll() and rx_start()/rx_poll(), backed by a real state machine (sdio_transfer_state_t SDIO_IDLE/RX/TX/TX_WAIT_IDLE, wr_status in rp2040_sdio.h:39-87). That is submit-then-poll -- driveable from a per-frame drainer without ever blocking. (5) WE ARE NOT ON IT: src/hw_config.c configures SD_IF_SPI on spi1 at 12.5 MHz (SCK 30 / MOSI 31 / MISO 40 / CS 43), matching the Waveshare demo -- i.e. the blocking 1-bit path.

CRITICAL CAVEAT that bounds the whole payoff: the dominant write latency is NOT transfer time, it is the card's internal program/erase, during which the card holds the line busy (can be 100 ms+). SDIO and DMA shorten the transfer; NEITHER shortens the erase. So SDIO cannot remove the need for PIZERO-65's queue -- at best it lets the drainer poll instead of spin, and moves bulk loads (ROM/DSK/wavetable reads) meaningfully faster. Do not let this ticket be mistaken for a fix for the write-stall problem.

SCOPE: (1) HARDWARE FEASIBILITY FIRST, before any code -- does this board's microSD socket even expose DAT1-DAT3? The vendor demo uses SPI (.ref/demo/RP2350-PiZero/Arduino/03-MicroSD/, C/03-MicroSD/), which is weak evidence the extra lines may not be wired; check docs/RP2350-PiZero-schematic.pdf. If they are not brought out, close this ticket -- that is a valid and cheap outcome. (2) PIN + PIO BUDGET AUDIT: SDIO needs CLK/CMD/DAT0-3 on suitable pins, and it is itself PIO-based, so it contends with libdvi (which already uses PIO with pio_set_gpio_base(pio,16) because TMDS is on GPIO 32-39) and Pico-PIO-USB (HOST_PIN_DP=28). Confirm free PIO state machines and instruction space, not just free GPIOs. (3) Verify carlk3's SDIO path actually supports RP2350 (the files are named rp2040_sdio.*) and works at our 252 MHz sys clock -- PIO timing is clock-derived, so this is a real risk, and the same clock-conflict class as the documented HSTX/DVI constraint. (4) MEASURE against the PIZERO-64 SPI baseline: sequential read throughput, single- and multi-block write, and worst-case write+sync stall. (5) Only if all the above pass, wire the start/poll API into the PIZERO-65 drainer so it polls rather than blocks, and consider keeping SPI as a build-flag fallback.

DECISION RULE (set now so this doesn't drift): if PIZERO-64 measures worst-case write+sync in the low tens of ms, SPI is adequate indefinitely and this ticket stays deferred. Pursue SDIO only if the measurements are bad, or if a later feature (PIZERO-17 synth wavetable streaming from flash/SD, large PIZERO-71 VFS files) needs the read bandwidth. Depends on PIZERO-64 for the baseline numbers; informs PIZERO-65 and PIZERO-70 (the backend interface should not assume a blocking transport).
